title: Span Gateway: OTLP fan-out adapter with signature normalization
creator: Asha Menon
description: Background: Our hosted tracing ingestion receives OTLP spans from SDKs and internal services. Customers and internal teams require the ability to forward the same traces to multiple backends (Tempo, Jaeger, external customer endpoints) while preserving semantic compatibility for legacy dashboards and downstream tooling. Problem: Directly fan-out raw OTLP results in inconsistent field signatures (status/code, tag keys, trace/span ID formats), high egress cost, and uneven backpressure behavior across sinks. Goal: Build a Span Gateway adapter that: 1) normalizes span signatures for Jaeger compatibility (legacy tag -> attribute mapping, status translation), 2) fans out to multiple backends with configurable per-sink transformations, 3) enforces tenant-aware rate limits and backpressure to protect latency SLOs, and 4) provides observability on fanout success/failure and per-tenant budget consumption. Scope: implement adapter logic, a transformation DSL for common mappings, tests, a gradual rollout plan, and dashboards/alerts. Non-goals: full reimplementation of exporters in every language and wire protocol; long-term saga-style guaranteed-delivery (we will provide best-effort with retries and DLQ for critical sinks).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts OTLP v0.9/1.0 proto and exposes a stable HTTP/GRPC endpoint documented in the internal API spec.
Transformation pipeline supports: status conversion (OTLP->Jaeger), tag/attribute renames, traceid/spanid zero-padding/hex normalization, and sampling flags propagation.
Fan-out path can target Tempo and legacy Jaeger collectors simultaneously for the same span without dropping required fields for either backend.
Per-tenant rate limiting enforced and configurable via Console; incidents show no SLO regressions during 95th/99th latency tests under target load (see perf criteria).
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering transformation rules, retry/backpressure behavior, and DLQ handling; e2e test harness exercise both Jaeger and Tempo endpoints.
Operational dashboards created: fanout success rate, per-sink latency, queue depth, DLQ counts, tenant throttle events.
design_decisions: Use a single Span Gateway service written in Go for low-latency proto handling and existing infra compatibility.
Apply transformation at ingestion time (in-memory) rather than downstream to minimize per-sink divergence and support consistent sampling metrics.
Design a small, declarative transformation DSL (YAML) mapping keys and rules so product/SEs can add simple conversions without code changes.
Backpressure strategy: prefer fast-fail with throttling + per-sink bounded queues rather than blocking upstream callers; provide auto-fallthrough to a lower-cost sink when configured.
Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter for transient errors; permanent failures go to per-tenant DLQ (S3) for diagnostics; do not retry indefinitely.
Privacy: strip or hash PII attributes by default via config flag; require security review for any rule that disables hashing.
Authentication: validate incoming API keys and tenant headers; route by tenant mapping table in config DB.
implementation_notes: Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/span-gateway (new service under observability org).
Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/span-gateway/pull/137 (basic OTLP ingestion + Tempo exporter).
Follow-up PRs: transformation DSL parser (#142), Jaeger exporter shim with signature normalization (#148), per-tenant rate limiter (#153).
Performance target: p95 end-to-end ingestion-to-export latency < 40ms under typical load; p99 < 150ms for non-bursty tenant workloads.
Use existing infra components where possible: envoy for ingress, redis for small per-tenant token buckets (bounded), s3 for DLQ storage.
Instrumentation: emit internal spans for gateway processing with tags for sink and rule_applied; create metric m.gateway.fanout_latency_ms and m.gateway.dlq_events.
Compatibility: include a compatibility test matrix converting OTLP semantic conventions to Jaeger tags used by legacy dashboards (see tests/compat_matrix.yaml).
Edge case: traceid length normalization (OTLP 128-bit vs older 64-bit Jaeger) -> choose hex lowercasing and zero-pad/truncate policy documented in design doc.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood - route <10% of internal non-prod traffic to new gateway and monitor errors/latency (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Beta customers - enable for select customers with enterprise agreements; collect feedback on legacy dashboards (4 weeks).
Phase 3: Gradual global rollouts by tenant group with circuit breakers - stepwise increase and manual gating via Console toggles.
Fallbacks: automatic fallback to single-sink mode if per-sink failure rate > 5% in 5m window; alert SRE and pause fanout for affected tenant.
Final: Default routing for new tenants after 90 days of stable telemetry and security sign-off.
test_plan: Unit tests for every transformation rule and DSL parser edge case.
Integration tests: run gateway against a real Tempo instance and a Jaeger/legacy collector in CI; validate exported payloads match golden fixtures.
Load tests: k6 scenario that simulates 10k spans/s with mixed sizes and checks latency SLOs; use synthetic tenants with varying quotas.
Chaos tests: introduce backend latency and failures to validate backpressure strategy and DLQ behavior.
Security tests: verify PII hashing and KMS access for DLQ encryption; complete security review checklist.
